name: Ma'mar ibn Rashid
nameAr: معمر بن راشد الأزدي الحُدّاني مولاهم أبو عروة البصري نزيل اليمن
bornNote: Reckoned from the Taqrib's statement that he died in 154 AH aged 58
diedNote: 154 AH in San'a (Taqrib); other reports range from 150 to 155

deathVariants.authority: other reports collected in the rijal works

taqrib.ar: ثقة ثبت فاضل، إلا أن في روايته عن ثابت والأعمش وعاصم بن أبي النجود وهشام بن عروة شيئا، وكذا فيما حدث به بالبصرة
taqrib.en: Reliable, firm and virtuous, except that there is something in his transmission from Thabit, al-A'mash, Asim ibn Abi al-Najud and Hisham ibn Urwa, and likewise in what he narrated at Basra.

role: One of the foremost transmitters of al-Zuhri; teacher of Abd al-Razzaq in San'a

verdicts.en: Ma'mar ibn Rashid, the reliable and trustworthy; al-Nasa'i placed him in the first class of al-Zuhri's companions.

verdicts.ar: لا تضم معمرا إلى أحد إلا وجدت معمرا أطلب للعلم منه، وهو أول من رحل إلى اليمن
verdicts.en: Set Ma'mar beside anyone and you will find Ma'mar the keener seeker of knowledge; he was the first to travel to Yemen for it.

verdicts.ar: ما حدث معمر بالبصرة ففيه أغاليط، وهو صالح الحديث
verdicts.en: What Ma'mar narrated at Basra contains errors; he is acceptable in hadith.

verdicts.ar: انتهى الإسناد إلى ستة نفر أدركهم معمر وكتب عنهم، لا أعلم اجتمع لأحد غير معمر: من الحجاز الزهري وعمرو بن دينار، ومن الكوفة أبو إسحاق والأعمش، ومن البصرة قتادة، ومن اليمامة يحيى بن أبي كثير
verdicts.en: The chains of transmission came down to six men, all of whom Ma'mar met and wrote from; I know of no one but Ma'mar who gathered them all: from the Hijaz al-Zuhri and Amr ibn Dinar, from Kufa Abu Ishaq and al-A'mash, from Basra Qatada, and from al-Yamama Yahya ibn Abi Kathir.

verdicts.ar: بصري سكن اليمن، ثقة، رجل صالح
verdicts.en: A Basran who settled in Yemen; reliable, a righteous man.

verdicts.ar: سمعت ابن معين يقدم مالك بن أنس على أصحاب الزهري ثم معمرا، قال: ومعمر عن ثابت ضعيف
verdicts.en: I heard Ibn Ma'in put Malik ibn Anas first among al-Zuhri's companions, then Ma'mar; and he said: Ma'mar from Thabit is weak.

dhahabi.ar: وقال أحمد: لا تضم معمرا إلى أحد إلا وجدته يتقدمه، كان من أطلب أهل زمانه للعلم
dhahabi.en: Al-Dhahabi quotes Ahmad: set Ma'mar beside anyone and you find him ahead; he was among the keenest seekers of knowledge of his time.

flags.label: Weaker in his Basran teaching and from four teachers
flags.detail: The critics distinguish what Ma'mar taught in Yemen, from his books, from what he dictated from memory on visits to Basra; and they mark his transmission from Thabit, al-A'mash, Asim and Hisham ibn Urwa as less firm. From al-Zuhri he is among the very best. In this hadith Ibn al-Mubarak joins him to Yunus and uses Yunus's wording, so nothing rests on Ma'mar's words alone.

bio: A Basran client of al-Azd who travelled young, heard al-Zuhri in the Hijaz, and settled in San'a, where the Yemenis married him off so that he would not leave; Abd al-Razzaq's Musannaf preserves much of his teaching. Abu Hatim notes that he alone met all six men on whom the chains of his generation converged. Ibn al-Mubarak said his hadith and Yunus's seemed to come from a single lamp.

provenance.ref: Shamela narrator record 6279, drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal 28/303, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 4/125 and Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal 11/300
al-Kashif 4/321, as quoted on the Shamela record
Chains of Sahih al-Bukhari 6, 3220 and Sahih Muslim 2308
